title: SAML session token-binding, audit-enrichment, and admin-initiated rekey orchestration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We currently depend on opaque session tokens issued after SAML handshake and JIT provisioning. This leads to ambiguous audit trails (missing RBAC context), difficulty enforcing admin-initiated rekey/revoke across devices, and unclear MFA expectations on step-up.

Goal: Implement a token-binding and audit-enrichment layer for SAML sessions that: (1) ties session tokens to SAML assertion metadata and optional device fingerprinting, (2) surfaces RBAC v2 role/context in audit logs, and (3) supports an orchestrated admin-initiated rekey/revoke flow (graceful logout, tombstone state, and forced reauth/step-up). Must be compatible with major IdPs and preserve privacy settings for customers that opt out of device fingerprinting.
acceptance_criteria: Session tokens include irreversible token-binding to SAML assertion ID (InResponseTo) and short-lived nonce; tokens must be verifiable by the runtime without storing raw assertions.

Audit logs record: SAML issuer, InResponseTo, JIT provisioned user id, RBAC v2 role snapshot, MFA level at issuance, and admin-revoke event ids. All fields are indexed where feasible for searching in the Console.

Admin-initiated rekey flow: admin can trigger a revoke that places sessions into a tombstone state, returning 401 with a reauth hint; users performing step-up are routed to MFA flow and re-bound tokens on success.
Backward compatibility: Sessions created before rollout continue to be accepted but annotated with legacy flag; new enforcement (forced rebind on sensitive routes) can be toggled via feature flag.
End-to-end test coverage and integration tests with Okta and Azure AD SAML test tenants are implemented and passing in CI.
Security review completed and KMS rotation tested with no downtime in staging.
implementation_notes: Add token-binding header: derive HMAC(inresponseTo + nonce) using per-tenant key stored in KMS; only HMAC stored in session store to avoid PII exposure.
Extend audit event schema: add fields saml_issuer, saml_inresponse_to, jit_user_id, rbac_v2_snapshot, mfa_level, admin_action_id. Ensure these are emitted for session create/renew/revoke.
Introduce 'tombstone' session state: tombstone TTL default 5 minutes (configurable). Tombstoned sessions return 401 with X-Reauth-Hint and admin_action_id header for traceability.

Step-up orchestration: on protected route, if policy requires step-up, return 403 with step-up challenge id. On successful MFA (IdP or Redwood-managed), issue new token bound to assertion and record mfa_level.
Feature flags: sessions.token_binding.enabled, sessions.tombstone.enabled, sessions.audit.enrichment.enabled, sessions.legacy_accept.enabled.
Privacy opt-out: customers can set tenant.setting.device_fingerprint = false; when false, only assertion-based binding used (no device fingerprinting).
test_plan: Unit tests for HMAC derivation with mocked KMS keys; assert no raw assertion data stored.
Integration tests: Okta and Azure AD SAML end-to-end provisioning, log ingestion verification in Console staging logs, RBAC snapshot correctness across role changes.
Chaos test: admin revoke while active streaming connection exists; verify graceful fallback and token invalidation on reconnect.
Security tests: replay attack simulation where assertion ID is reused; ensure token-binding prevents reuse.
Performance test: measure token verification latency added by HMAC verify under 1ms median at p50 on runtime-1.24 config.
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): Enable token-binding and audit enrichment for internal tenants only. Monitor auth latency, console log volume, and false-positive reauth triggers.
Week 2 (beta): Open to selected customers via opt-in tenant flag; collect feedback and fix edge-cases with legacy SAML responses.
Week 3 (gradual): Flip legacy_accept to false behind tenant migration plan; enable tombstone enforcement on sensitive admin routes first.
Rollback: toggle sessions.token_binding.enabled=false or revert to accepting legacy tokens while investigating. All admin actions are reversible through admin_action_id audit link.
comments: 2025-11-06 - Aisha Kumar: Initial triage and scope agreed with SecEng. We need to ensure KMS throughput will support HMAC ops at peak — reached out to infra for capacity estimates.

2025-11-10 - Marco Chen: Spike completed. Derived approach uses per-tenant symmetric key and HMAC-SHA256 on (InResponseTo || nonce). Prototype shows ~0.6ms median verify time on g4dn-staging. PR#1845 created.

2025-11-12 - Security review (Elena Park): Requested explicit threat model for assertion replay and guidance for opt-out. Also requested encryption-at-rest confirmation for session store fingerprints. Assigned SEC-314 for follow-up.

2025-11-14 - Product feedback (Samir Patel): Console needs a filter for 'admin_action_id' and the ES mapping change; added task for console team and linked PR. Also asked for changelog language for customers about reauth hints.

2025-11-16 - Marco Chen: Implemented tombstone flow and exposed admin_action_id in audit events. Adding integration tests for Okta. Noted two IdP responses include different InResponseTo formats — added normalization step.

2025-11-18 - QA (Jing Li): Integration tests passing in staging for Okta and Azure AD. Found edge case: some IdPs omit AuthnContext; we record null mfa_level and enforce step-up only on policy. Logged follow-up ENG-83045.
notes: Trade-offs: token-binding increases token verification cost and audit volume. We limit stored fields and HMAC-derived tokens to balance privacy and searchability. Device fingerprinting is optional to respect customer privacy.
